Brief Review

An insurance investigator for a cyborg manufacturer looks into the destruction of a robot by a police officer claiming the robot was repairing its self, which was never supposed to be possible.

Story

In the 2030's, massive solar flairs irradiated the Earth and killed off 99% of the world's population. The ROC corporation built humanoid robots to handle the tasks that need to be done outside in the extreme radiation. These robots were programmed to be servants and nothing more, until in 2044, on a routine patrol, Officer Wallace discovers a robot attempting to repair its self, which it is not programmed to do, and he promptly shoots it until it stops functioning. Jacq Vaucan is assigned the job of investigating the report that the robot was violating its programming. He finds a nuclear battery that is able to power a robot indefinitely and this leads him down a rabbit hole of trying to find how these robots are appearing to perform and live outside of their programming.

What Was Good

The first half of the movie was very intriguing. The cyber-punk-esque world that was created gave a good glimpse of the world like similar titles (Blade Runner, Virtual Revolution, etc). The story, while not new, had an interesting spin with Jacq and his wife trying to plan for the future now that her pregnancy is almost to due, which was also rare since the radiation also affected fertility of the remaining 1% of the population. The investigation was also done well, with Jacq meeting new robots along the way, each one seeming to act on their own, without the command of an owner.

What Was Bad

The pacing of the movie suffers greatly after Jacq leaves the city limits. The character of Sean Wallace was over the top douchebag, to the point that I hoped Jacq would just shoot him instead and continue on without his help. While I think Antonio Banderas is a decent actor, at times his accent was too thick and I found myself rewinding just to better make out what he was trying to say. I hated how they portrayed the majority of humans as being assholes, but Jacq was the only kind heart trying to do the right thing, how ROC ignored all AI advancement possibilities and instantly called for Jacq's head on a spike for even daring to question their programming might have flaws. The scientist would be intrigued by AI becoming self aware, but not in this world, fuck it, burn it all to the ground! Highly unbelievable.

Final Thoughts

This is another classic example of a movie with promise starts off solid, can hook the viewer, proposes some deep philosophical questions, and then half way through the movie makes you want to slit your own wrists just to make it end sooner. It almost felt like after Jacq fled from the city that they didn't know how to continue and just starting throwing darts at a board. This is definitely one to skip, you aren't missing much. The only people who might find some enjoyment are die hard cyber-punk fans, and even then, one or two viewings are all they would need before shelfing it forever. If there's nothing better on, it will kill 2 hours for you, but don't be pissed when you feel like you want those 2 hours back.
